name: Accent Builder
description: The resonance and the accent at their tops and little envelope, so plain notes stay dark and accents leap: play accents in a row and each one sings higher than the last.

name: Bright Acid
description: The filter higher and the resonance strong: a bright line that cuts through a full mix.

name: Chirp
description: The envelope at its top with a short decay and the resonance high: each step a quick chirp falling from the top.

name: Classic Squelch
description: The saw through a resonant filter that the envelope snaps open and lets fall: the squelching line the instrument is known for. Accented notes bark and whistle, and accents in a row build.

name: Dark Rumble
description: The saw an octave down, the filter almost shut and a long decay, through the overdrive: a dark, growling rumble.

name: Deep Bass
description: The square through a filter low and nearly closed, with little envelope and no resonance: a round, deep bass that sits under a mix. Accents only lean on it.

name: Distorted Square
description: The square squelch into the distortion pedal's circuit, its tone dark: a fat, buzzing line.

name: Fuzz Bass
description: The saw through a filter left fairly open with little resonance, into the distortion pedal's circuit: a fuzz bass for patterns that want weight more than squelch.

name: Hollow Square
description: The square through a filter left open with a little resonance and envelope: a hollow, reedy bass that keeps its edges.

name: Low Acid
description: The squelch an octave down, the filter a little lower: a deep acid line that is half bass.

name: Muted Acid
description: The filter low and the decay short, the resonance up: dark, ticking steps that only the accents open.

name: Open Acid
description: A long decay and a lot of envelope, so the filter barely closes between steps: a washy, open acid line for long builds.

name: Overdriven Square
description: The square through a resonant filter into the overdrive pedal's circuit, which thickens its middle: a warm, gritty bass.

name: Plucked Blip
description: The shortest decay and the envelope at its top, through a resonant filter left low: each note a short, plucked blip.

name: Rave Acid
description: The saw with the resonance and envelope high into the overdrive pedal's circuit: a hard, singing line for fast tracks.

name: Rolling Saw
description: The saw with a short decay and a middling resonance: tight sixteenths that roll along, each step clicking and gone before the next.

name: Rubber Bass
description: The square through a half-resonant filter that pops open at each note and settles quickly: a bouncy, rubbery bass.

name: Screaming Acid
description: The squelch at full resonance and envelope, driven hard into the distortion pedal's circuit: a screaming, distorted acid line whose accents tear.

name: Slide Line
description: A long decay and a resonant filter that stays open through tied notes, for lines played legato: every note struck before the last one ends glides into its pitch without striking the envelope again.

name: Soft Acid
description: The saw through a filter with half the resonance and a little envelope: a gentle, rounded acid line for quieter tracks.

name: Square Squelch
description: The square through the filter near its singing, snapped open at each step: a hollow, rubbery squelch.

name: Steady Acid
description: Little accent and a moderate resonance: an even line in which every step sounds alike, for patterns that carry their own shape.

name: High Acid
description: The squelch an octave up, bright and singing, sliding where the notes tie: an acid lead over a bass line.

name: Resonant Lead
description: The saw an octave up, the resonance nearly at its top and a long decay, so the filter sings over each note: a whistling lead that glides where notes overlap.

name: Whistle Acid
description: The square an octave up with the resonance at its top and a long decay: the filter whistles over every step, the accents shrieking.
